questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime, policy-driven security for multi-tenant clusters, including per-tenant exceptions, scalable policy storage, and practical CI validation.

## Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Rego enforcement
- Runtime security: runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, hostPath, privileged, SETUID checks
- Central PolicyStore for per-tenant overrides
- CI validation: dry-run, Gatekeeper evaluation, and manifest validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: runtimepolicy
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: RuntimePolicy
        listKind: RuntimePolicyList
        plural: runtimepolicies
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package runtimepolicy
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
        msg := "container must run as non-root"
      }
      violation[{"msg": msg}]
      {
        any_cont := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not any_cont.securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "container must have readOnlyRootFilesystem: true"
      }
      # Additional rules for hostPath, privileged, and SETUID would follow similarly
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of identity-based runtime access control in Kubernetes, integrating SPIRE, OPA Gatekeeper, and admission/mutating webhooks for auditing. It also evaluates plan for cross-cloud (Snowflake/IBM) data workloads and secure Spark job execution.

## Key Concepts
- SPIRE workload identity and attestation
- OPA Gatekeeper constraint templates and validation hooks
- Kubernetes RBAC and API access control
- Mutating webhook for audit sidecars
- Validation strategy with compliant vs noncompliant pods

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (example): OPA-based API access gate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapiaiaccess
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sAPIAccess
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |-
      package k8sapiaiaccess
      violate["API access denied: identity not whitelisted"] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        identity := input.review.object.metadata.annotations["spire.identity"]
        not identity_in_allowlist(identity)
      }
      
      # allowlisted identities (simplified)
      identity_in_allowlist(id) {
        id == "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
      }
```

```yaml
# Compliant Pod (SPIRE-identity annotated)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: compliant-spark
  annotations:
    spire.identity: "spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/spark-sa"
spec:
  serviceAccountName: spark-sa
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Pod (no SPIRE identity)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: noncompliant-spark
spec:
  containers:
  - name: spark
    image: myrepo/spark:latest
```

## Validation Plan
- Deploy constraint template and constraint; attempt compliant pod deployment; verify admission allows and audit sidecar is injected. 
- Deploy noncompliant pod; confirm admission denies with clear event reason. 
- Run a Spark job and inspect API calls logged by the auditing sidecar for traceability.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to enforce Kubernetes scheduling best practices through automated CI gates. It demonstrates understanding of pod distribution for high availability, GitOps workflows, and infrastructure-as-code validation.

## Key Concepts

- **Kubernetes topologySpreadConstraints**: Controls how pods are distributed across failure domains (zones, nodes, etc.)
- **Deployment replicas and scaling**: Understanding when and why to distribute workloads
- **YAML parsing in CI pipelines**: Using Python or Node.js to validate manifests
- **GitHub Actions workflow configuration**: Building automated gates for GitOps
- **Local validation and pre-commit hooks**: Catching issues before code reaches CI

## Code Example

```python
# gate-topology.py
import sys
import yaml
import glob

def check_deploymentConstraints(doc):
    if doc.get('kind') != 'Deployment':
        return True
    
    replicas = doc.get('spec', {}).get('replicas', 1)
    if replicas <= 2:
        return True
    
    topology = doc.get('spec', {}).get('template', {}).get('spec', {})
    if 'topologySpreadConstraints' not in topology:
        return False
    
    for constraint in topology['topologySpreadConstraints']:
        if constraint.get('topologyKey') != 'topology.kubernetes.io/zone':
            return False
        maxSkew = constraint.get('maxSkew', 1)
        if maxSkew > 1:
            return False
    
    return True

def main():
    failed = []
    for manifest in glob.glob('**/*.yaml', recursive=True):
        with open(manifest) as f:
            docs = yaml.safe_load_all(f)
            for doc in docs:
                if doc and not check_deploymentConstraints(doc):
                    failed.append(manifest)
    
    if failed:
        print(f"Failing manifests: {failed}")
        sys.exit(1)
    
    print("All Deployments pass topology constraints check")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## GitHub Actions Workflow

```yaml
name: Topology Constraints Gate
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  enforce-topology:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pip install pyyaml
      - name: Run topology gate
        run: python gate-topology.py
```

## Failing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:latest
```

## Passing Manifest Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: web
      containers:
      - name: web
        image: nginx:latest
```

## How to Verify

**Local Verification:**
```bash
pip install pyyaml
python gate-topology.py
```

**CI Verification:**
The GitHub Actions workflow runs automatically on pull requests. Merges are blocked until all Deployments with replicas > 2 include proper topologySpreadConstraints.

**Pre-commit Hook:**
Add to `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
```yaml
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: topology-gate
        name: Enforce topologySpreadConstraints
        entry: python gate-topology.py
        language: system
        types: [yaml]
```

## Why This Is Asked


```yaml
# passing manifest (PDB + readOnlyRootFilesystem: true)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: svc-a
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-reg/app-a@sha256:abc
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: pdb-svc-a
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:

      app: svc-a
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate (minimal)
name: PDB + ReadOnlyRootFilesystem gate
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
jobs:
  ck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: 'latest'
      - name: Lint manifests
        run: |
          kubectl version --client
          echo 'Lint step placeholder for yamllint/jsonlint'
      - name: Validate PDB and readOnlyRootFilesystem
        run: |
          # simple validation example
          if ! kubectl get pdb pdb-svc-a >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo 'PDB missing for svc-a'; exit 1
          fi
          if ! grep -R "readOnlyRootFilesystem: true" -n k8s || true; then
            echo 'Some container not enforcing readOnlyRootFilesystem'; exit 1
          fi
```

## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant clusters need strict API access control; SPIFFE identity ensures only trusted services can perform sensitive calls. Gatekeeper + OPA enforces runtime policy with centralized visibility.

## Key Concepts
- OPA Gatekeeper
- ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- SPIFFE IDs and SVIDs
- Kubernetes API verbs and RBAC implications
- Validation via audit logs and Gatekeeper status

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sapicnst
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sApiConstraint
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
      rego: |
        package k8sapi
        violation[{"msg": msg}] {
          input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
          input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
          not allowed_spiffe(input.review.object)
          msg := sprintf("Pod %s in namespace %s cannot use API verb %s", [input.review.object.metadata.name, input.review.object.metadata.namespace, input.review.operation])
        }
        allowed_spiffe(pod) {
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"]
          pod.metadata.annotations["spiffe.io/spiffe-id"] in data.constraint.spec.allowedSVIDs
        }
```

```yaml
# Constraint
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sApiConstraint
metadata:
  name: restrict-api-verbs
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  allowedSVIDs:
    - "spiffe://ibm.com/workload/web"
    - "spiffe://tesla.com/workload/monitor"
    - "spiffe://cloudflare.com/workload/edge"
```

## Validation Plan
1. Deploy ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
2. Test compliant GET request from approved SPIFFE ID
3. Test noncompliant POST request from unapproved SPIFFE ID
4. Verify denial in Gatekeeper audit logs
5. Confirm monitoring namespace bypass works correctly

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's practical understanding of security and governance gating for Infrastructure as Code (IaC). It tests knowledge of:

- Terraform IaC fundamentals and best practices
- Static analysis security scanning with tfsec
- Custom linting rules with tflint
- GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline configuration
- Secrets management best practices in CI environments

## Key Concepts

**tfsec**: A static analysis security scanner for Terraform code that detects hard-coded credentials, insecure configurations, and common infrastructure vulnerabilities before deployment. It scans for secrets embedded in code and flags misconfigurations that could lead to security breaches.

**tflint**: A extensible linter for Terraform that enforces organization-specific policies. It can be configured with custom rules to ensure consistency across infrastructure code, such as requiring standardized tags on all resources for billing, ownership tracking, and environment classification.

## What Success Looks Like

A strong answer demonstrates:
- Understanding of how tfsec catches secrets at scan time
- Knowledge of tflint's rule configuration for tag enforcement
- Familiarity with GitHub Secrets integration in CI/CD
- Ability to write practical, working Terraform configurations
- Awareness of local vs. CI validation workflows

This combination of skills is essential for maintaining secure, compliant infrastructure at scale.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests extending supply-chain checks to edge with hardware attestation.

## Key Concepts
- Edge TPM attestation
- Image signing and SBOM attestations
- Rekor / transparency log
- OPA/Kyverno admission policies

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Kyverno policy snippet (illustrative)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-edge-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: require-attested-node
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: [Deployment]
    validate:
      message: "Node must be TPM-attested and image signed."
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              nodeSelector:
                edge_attested: "true"
```
